members.note: FDreamInputKeySelectorStyle: the button's five state colours plus the sixth this control needs -- Listening, which is the whole of the 'press a key now' feedback.
The label's colour and size are FDreamInputKeySelectorStyle::LabelColor and FontSize; this library does not split a control's look into a button style and a text style.

UMG's SelectedKey IS an FInputChord, so the chord is the faithful mapping. This control also carries a bare-FKey SelectedKey as the compatibility spelling existing .dui authors, kept coherent through every writer.
Space around the key's name. Appearance, so it lives in the style struct.
SetKeySelectionText carries the UMG name and forwards. Empty keeps the built-in words, so a project overrides the prompt without overriding the control.
SetNoKeySpecifiedText carries the UMG name and forwards.
Only the CAPTURE path reads it: NotifyKeyPressed and NotifyChordPressed are fed by a caller that already knows what was held.

On by default, which is what the capture agent already did. Off, a pad key is neither bound nor CONSUMED -- it was meant for something else, and swallowing it would leave a controller doing nothing while a selector is armed. The escape keys are checked first, so the pad's B is still a way out.
Seeded with Escape and the pad's B. Emptying it is legal and means the click is the only way out, which the header documents as a trap.
UMG's carries an FInputChord, which is OnChordSelected here. This control also fires OnKeySelected with the bare key from the same moment, for a consumer that only cares which key.
Carries the new state, where UMG's carries nothing -- a handler that dims the rest of the screen needs to know which way it went.
UMG's takes an FInputChord. SetSelectedKey exists here too and takes a bare FKey, which CLEARS any modifiers: 'bind exactly this key' is what a caller of the key-shaped setter is saying.
Forwards to SetListeningText, which re-labels at once.
The armed state under UMG's name; GetIsListening is the library's own spelling of the same flag.

Takes EDreamWidgetVisibility, this library's own five answers for the same question. The LABEL only: the face keeps its visibility, so the selector stays clickable, which is the documented way out of the armed state.
